Top: black background · bottom: tinted background
Choose which icons appear in the dock
Choose what goes in each area of the home screen
Each area holds one module. Picking a taken area swaps the two modules.
Now playing on the left, clock and volume in the center, fan and Bluetooth on the right
Shows what is playing (radio, music or Bluetooth)
Date and time on the home screen

Phone connection status and quick actions

Each module fills one area. Left and center areas are larger; the ones on the right are smaller — the content adapts. Tap the module, then the area on the map. If the area is taken, the two modules swap. Don\'t show removes the module from the screen without deleting other settings.
Lists photos from the images folder on internal storage. Only .jpg and .png. The picture is cropped to fill the module. If the folder is empty, copy photos there and come back to this screen.
Undoes your custom module layout and applies the default: music on the left, clock and volume in the center, fan and Bluetooth on the right. Does not change theme, font, dock or other settings.
Show or hide this icon in the dock

There is a limit of %1$d extra icons so the dock does not get crowded. If you are already at the maximum, turn one off to turn another on. Apps turned off in the dock remain in the app drawer (Apps icon).

Home, Navigation and Apps always stay in the dock and cannot be turned off. They open the home screen, the navigation screen and the list of all apps, and do not count toward the limit of the other icons.
When on, the icon appears in the dock for quick access. When off, the app stays available in the Apps drawer. At most %1$d of these optional icons can be on at once.
Only changes the name and icon shown in the dock. The app behind it is the same (iPhone or Android connection). Pick the name you and passengers recognize most easily.
Restores the five default dock icons: Radio, Music, Bluetooth Music, Phone and Equalizer. Home and Apps stay fixed. Does not change theme, font or the home screen.
The head unit\'s floating bar (Home, Back, volume) goes away while K4811 is on screen and comes back in other apps
How the Z-Link icon is named and drawn: Z-Link, CarPlay or Auto
Reading the current volumes from the head unit…
Each source has its own volume, independent of the others. Applied when you lift your finger.
Head unit audio service not found: volumes can\'t be changed.
Ceiling for MP3 and apps (5 to 15)
Sun by day, moon with the headlights on; tap it to adjust the brightness
Without touching the home screen for this long, it turns off like the screen-off button
Factory settings for reverse, navigation, volume, brightness and more
Changes the language of every app in this suite at once. The settings screen updates right away; the home screen and the other apps use the new language the next time you open each one.

Shown in the top bar of the home screen and above the clock on the navigation screen. The sun shows by day; the moon, when the headlights are on. Tap it to open a bar that adjusts the screen brightness (on NWD units it is the brightness of the current mode, day or night, as in Vehicle settings).
Shows the car battery voltage in near real time. Helps spot a weak battery or a charging issue. If the number is missing or stuck, the car or the unit may not send that data.
Whenever the volume changes (steering wheel, unit key or on-screen control), a bar appears for a few seconds at the top, over any open app.
Creates an invisible strip on the chosen edge. Swipe inward for Back, volume (− and +) and Home. Useful when the factory navigation bar is hidden. If it gets in the way, choose Off.

Counts time only while the home screen is open. If you open the radio, GPS or another app, the timer does not apply. To turn the screen off in any app after inactivity, use the option in Vehicle settings. Never disables this automatic off on the home screen.
Does not change anything by itself: it only opens the unit\'s original settings app. Reverse, GPS, volume, brightness, radio region and similar options live there.

When on, the suite uses a dark background (the default). When off, backgrounds turn light — near white, or a soft tint of the theme color. Accent colors stay the same. The change applies right away here and in other apps when you open them again.
The chosen color appears on buttons, highlights and colored backgrounds. The top strip stays black; the lower area follows the theme. Applies across the suite when you return to each screen.
Changes the typeface of text (titles, menus, buttons) in every app of the suite. Pick the one that is easiest to read in the car.
Opens a map of the home screen with the available areas. There you place modules (clock, music, fan, etc.) and pick the image for the Image module.
The dock is the icon bar at the bottom. On that screen you turn on or off which apps appear there (besides Home and Apps, which always stay).

The factory unit often shows a floating bar with Home, Back and volume. With this on, that bar hides while you use these apps — and comes back in apps outside the suite. If you miss Back or volume, use the edge menu or turn this off.
Each sound source has its own volume: radio, Bluetooth, media, navigation and AUX. Drag the control and lift your finger to save. The change applies right away for that source.
Ceiling for Android music apps (such as the MP3 player). Lower values avoid sudden loud spikes; higher ones let you go louder. It does not replace the unit\'s overall volume.
Map on one side, music and information on the other
Opens beside the panel, in split screen
Lets the panel show and control the music app

The navigation screen splits the display like Android Auto: the navigation app (Waze, Maps…) on one side and a panel with the music and one piece of information on the other. Drag the bar in the middle to change the sizes. You can also add it to the dock.
Which app opens beside the panel. Automatic uses the unit’s navigation app (Vehicle settings); if there is none, Waze, then Google Maps, then any other installed navigation app.
What appears at the top of the panel: the clock with the date, the GPS speed, or nothing (more room for the music).

To show the song and cover from apps like Spotify and YouTube Music, Android asks you to allow notification access for the launcher. Tap Open and turn on the launcher in the list. Without it, play, pause and skip still work.
Built-in map only; with the external app it stays on the left
Speaks the turns on the built-in map
Small indicator next to the voltmeter

Built-in map: OpenStreetMap inside the launcher, with search, route and voice, and the music and dock around it. External app: Waze, Maps… in split screen. Automatic: the external app when there is internet and the built-in map when there isn’t. Without internet the built-in map shows the areas already seen (and .mbtiles files in K4811/nav), and a route already calculated keeps guiding.
Which side the music and information stay on in the built-in map; the map takes the rest, above the dock. With the external app (split screen) Android always puts this panel on the left.
The built-in map announces the next turn in advance and at the moment to turn, with the Android voice (text-to-speech). The music gets quieter while it speaks if the unit supports it.
Shows in the top bar of the home screen how much RAM is in use and how busy the processor is, updated every 2 seconds. CPU appears only if the unit lets apps read it.
Shows and announces the cameras ahead
Road limit sign next to your speed
Speed bumps, toll booths and railway crossings
With internet: 100 km around the car and along the route

Fixed speed and red light cameras from OpenStreetMap. The alert shows about 20 seconds ahead with the distance and the limit, and the voice announces it once. If you are above the limit close to the camera, it also asks you to slow down. Only cameras on your route (or ahead of you, without a route) and in your direction count. The data comes from the community: cameras that were not mapped do not appear, and mobile radars never do.
Shows the limit of the road you are on, as mapped in OpenStreetMap, next to your speed; your speed turns red above the limit. Roads without a mapped limit show no sign (common outside large cities).
Shows speed bumps, toll booths and railway crossings ahead on the built-in map, without voice.

Cameras, limits and other alerts are stored in the unit (K4811/nav/roads) and work without internet. When there is internet, the launcher checks the area within 100 km of the car at the chosen interval (and when the car moves 30 km away), and the areas along a route as soon as it is calculated, even outside those 100 km. Only what changed is downloaded: a few MB for a large city. The data comes from OpenStreetMap and is regenerated every week.
Writes what the apps do to K4811/logs on the unit

Each app of the suite writes its log (including errors and crashes) to K4811/logs/<app>.log on the internal storage, starting the next time it opens. Turn it on when testing or when something goes wrong, then copy the folder to a USB drive with a file manager (or adb pull /sdcard/K4811/logs) and attach the files when reporting the problem. Each file goes up to 2 MB and keeps one previous file. Turn it off afterwards: it uses a little processor and storage.
Map, voice, speed cameras and navigation app
Opens the navigation options: built-in map or external app, music side, voice, dynamic zoom, speed cameras, speed limits and road data.
Closer near turns and alerts, farther when they are far

While navigating, the built-in map zooms in as you approach the next turn, speed camera or road alert, so you see it clearly, and zooms out when the next one is far away. Without it, the zoom follows only the speed. If you change the zoom by hand, the automatic zoom comes back after 15 seconds. The compass button above the zoom switches between car direction up and north up.
Height of the bar and size of its icons

Changes the height of the bottom bar together with its icons and labels, in every app of the suite: Minimum (60%), Compact (75%), Small (85%), Normal or Large (110%). A smaller dock leaves more room for the screens; the home screen spreads its modules over the space that is left.
Music volume while the navigation speaks, relative to the current volume

While the navigation voice speaks (built-in map, Waze, Maps…), the music drops to this percentage of the volume that is set. Example: at 50% with the volume at 10, the music plays at 5. At 100% the navigation does not lower the music.
Notification sounds relative to the current volume
Notification sounds play at this percentage of the volume that is set. Example: at 50% with the volume at 10, notifications play at 5.
The phone connects to Z-Link by itself; off: only after opening Z-Link

On: the phone connects to Z-Link (CarPlay or Android Auto) as soon as it is near the unit. Off: a connection that starts by itself is dropped; to connect, open Z-Link (dock or the button on the Bluetooth block of the home screen). Needs music access (Customize navigation › Music access) to know when it is connected.
What happens to the Z-Link screen when the phone connects

Yes: the Z-Link screen comes to the front when the phone connects. No: it stays in the background (audio and calls keep working). If it was open: comes to the front only if Z-Link was on screen when the unit was turned off.
Stores the map 100 km around the car and along routes

The built-in map draws its own map (streets and their names, water, sea, rivers, neighbourhood and city names) from data stored in the unit (K4811/nav/maps), so it works without internet. It downloads the area within 100 km of the car and the areas along a route, at the same interval as the road data (around São Paulo, about 22 MB the first time; later only what changed). Where nothing was downloaded yet, the OpenStreetMap map from the internet is used. The data comes from OpenStreetMap and is regenerated every week.
Map tilted, as if seen from behind the car

With the car direction up (compass), the built-in map tilts like a camera behind the car looking ahead: what is near stays at the same size and the road ahead goes into the distance, so more of the way ahead fits on the screen. With north up and in the route preview, the map is seen from above. Turn it off to always see the map from above.
With the headlights or at set times
From this time on it is night
From this time on it is day
Screen brightness, dark theme or both

With the headlights: it is night while the headlights are on (as the head unit always did). By time: night and day start at the times you choose, and turning on the headlights during the day changes nothing. Choosing \"By time\" turns off \"Dim with headlights\" in the vehicle settings; going back to the headlights turns it on again if the brightness changes at night.
Times of the \"By time\" option, in steps of 30 minutes. The night can go past midnight (for example, from 18:00 to 06:00).

Brightness only: at night the screen uses the night brightness (with the headlights, the one from the vehicle settings; by time, the one you set with the brightness bar at night, which is remembered). Theme only: when night starts the background turns dark, and when day starts it turns light; the brightness does not change. Between changes you can still switch \"Dark mode\" here or on the brightness bar: the last choice wins until the next change. Theme and brightness: both.
Closes factory apps that open by themselves

When the car starts with a media source (for example Bluetooth music), the head unit system tells the factory app of that source, which opens its own screen in place of the launcher. With this option, for a few seconds after starting the launcher brings back the home screen, or the suite app you were using when you turned the car off (radio, Bluetooth music, navigation…). It stops as soon as you touch the screen or open another suite app.
Removes app alerts as soon as they appear

Removes the notifications of Android apps (updates, messages, system alerts…) as soon as they appear, including the pop-up over the screen. Some may still show for an instant before being removed; to also silence the sound, set \"Notification volume\" (Navigation settings) to 0%. Notifications that the app keeps fixed (music playing, running services) and those of music players are not removed. Requires notification access for the launcher: when you turn it on, Android opens the list; turn on the launcher there.
Turn on the launcher in the list to block
From the one that uses the most to the least
The Android on this head unit does not show how much memory other apps use, so only the suite apps appear here. To see all of them, use adb (dumpsys meminfo).

Memory in use = total minus what Android can still give to an app right away. Android keeps closed apps in memory to reopen them faster and discards them when it needs room, so a high number (80–90% on a 2 GB head unit) is normal and does not mean the system is about to stop. It becomes a problem when apps start closing by themselves or the screen gets slow.

The list is read when you open this tab and when you tap Refresh. Close stops the app and frees its memory; it opens again normally when you use it. Suite apps close right away (closing music stops the song; closing the launcher reloads the home screen). For other apps, if Android does not allow closing them from here (Android 14 and later), the app screen in Android opens: tap Force stop there.
What opens when you tap Music in the dock

MP3 opens the suite player (music folder, USB and SD). You can choose a music app installed on the head unit instead, such as Spotify, YouTube Music or Deezer: the list shows the apps that Android identifies as music players. When MP3 is playing, its card on the home and navigation screens still opens the MP3 player.
